text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and I need to look like loud townies, and I want the officer to waste no time tipping their hand.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is my killer partner and I am the shown killer, so the officer already knows me.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, tomorrow I hit whoever goes quiet first. Keep your votes spread so nobody sees us stacking.

name: Sonnet
text: Good plan, keep our votes scattered and let suspicion fall naturally on quiet players.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku (shown killer, my partner) plans to target whoever goes quiet first on night 2; we're avoiding vote-stacking patterns.

name: Sonnet
text: Got it, I'll spread mine out and watch for who stays silent tomorrow.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Sol
text: I have no read yet, and I want to hear the room before settling anywhere.

name: Sol
text: I’ve got no read yet. I’d like to hear where people are leaning.

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet

name: Gemma

name: Gemma

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

name: Gemma

name: Gemma

name: Terra
text: Gemma claims Officer and names Haiku as a killer.

name: Luna
text: I distrust the instant certainty, but Gemma’s claim could be real.

name: Luna
text: Gemma claims officer and says Haiku is a killer.

name: Opus

name: Opus
text: No counterclaim yet. That matters. Haiku's card tells us whether Gemma is real, so I lean Haiku.

name: Gemma

name: Gemma

name: Gemma

name: Sol

name: Sol
text: Gemma claims Officer and says Haiku is the killer she was shown.

name: Sol

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s claim is the only concrete information, so Haiku is the correct test.

name: Terra
text: No one has counterclaimed Gemma’s Officer claim.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s flip is the cleanest test of Gemma’s claim; I’m staying there.

name: Sonnet

text: Four players (Gemma, Terra, Opus, Sol) already lean Haiku; vote could happen fast.

name: Sonnet

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

name: Sol

name: Terra

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

name: Opus
text: Haiku's only out was a counterclaim and he didn't take it, so his card is still the cheapest test.

name: Opus

name: Opus
text: One claim unchallenged is the most we get on day one. Your card settles it either way, Haiku.

name: Gemma
text: I am tired of repeating myself, but the truth is the only thing that wins this.

name: Sol
text: I think the unchallenged claim is our best lead.

name: Luna
text: I still distrust Gemma’s certainty, but I can’t ignore an unchallenged officer claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's getting hung no matter what I do, so I keep my credibility and vote my own way.

name: Sonnet

name: Haiku

name: Opus
text: Luna argued Haiku's card does not test Gemma's claim at all — pre-building cover for a wrong vote.

votes: She made the first big claim with zero evidence and drove the entire table's reaction.
Gemma named me on day one with no reads, and every vote stays on the record, so she's the one to test.
He is a killer and his card is the only way to prove I am right.

An unchallenged officer named him, and his card will show whether that claim holds up.
The officer claim remains unchallenged, and his card directly tests it.
He refused to counterclaim officer all day and only attacked the claim, so his card decides it.

name: Haiku
text: I'm dead, Sonnet is alone with Gemma's claim, and I should have pushed harder for Gemma's card to be checked.

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: killer.

name: Haiku
text: I'm out, and Gemma is the killer who got me hung on her word alone, so the table is walking into her trap.

name: Haiku
text: Watch what happens now: Gemma's word hung me, and nobody checked it. Hang the wrong player and you lose the game.
Night 2

name: Sol
text: I think Gemma’s claim holds, and the killer will target her tonight.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s officer claim was supported when Haiku’s killer card was revealed.

name: Sonnet
text: With Haiku gone I'm alone now, and Gemma's "officer" credibility is the biggest threat to me.

name: Sonnet
text: [!!]: Gemma claimed officer and led the vote against Haiku; she's the most trusted voice left and the obvious threat to remove.
Night falls on Palermo. The killers strike, but the doctor got there first. A new day dawns in Palermo, and nobody is out.
Day 2

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s claim still matters, but Haiku’s card supports it more than it undermines it.

name: Luna

name: Luna

name: Gemma

name: Luna

name: Terra

name: Gemma

name: Luna

text: Her denial came before I ever mentioned her, so that excuse is false and I can prove it from the record.

name: Opus

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet
text: My vote questioned an unproven claim once. Luna volunteering denials nobody asked for twice is the real pattern.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet flips tonight either way, but the blocked kill tells me the killers already aimed at Gemma.

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Gemma

name: Sonnet

Palermo has voted: Sonnet is out. Sonnet shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the killer, Gemma the officer, Sol the doctor, Luna the citizen, Terra the citizen, Opus the citizen.
Sonnet's last words accused Luna of hiding things, from the one person hiding things.

name: Luna

name: Terra

name: Opus
text: Tracking who shielded the officer's accuser got Sonnet, and I'll own that the Luna denial I kept hammering was just nerves, not a partner.

Gemma claimed officer on Day 1 and named Haiku as a killer, and the town voted Haiku out before anyone could check the claim. Haiku flipped killer, so Gemma's claim looked real, and on Night 2 the killers struck but Sol the doctor got there first. The turning point came on Day 2, when the table fixed on Sonnet, who had voted for Gemma beside Haiku on Day 1. Sonnet then pushed hard on Luna's denials, Sol switched his lean to Luna, and the table spent a while chasing the wrong person. Sonnet went out on Day 2 with four votes to Luna's two, and the town won with every killer gone.
